source.title: Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models
source.authors: Xin Dong; Y. Fu; Shizhe Diao; Wonmin Byeon; Zi-Jia Chen; A. Mahabaleshwarkar; Shih-Yang Liu; Matthijs Van Keirsbilck; Min-Hung Chen; Yoshi Suhara; Y. Lin; Jan Kautz; Pavlo Molchanov

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares language-model perplexity across different architectures at matched parameter counts and training settings. This conceptually tests whether architecture changes loss only slightly, but it does not test power-law scaling.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the Wiki and LMB perplexities for matched architecture comparisons in Tables 3 and 9. Other benchmark accuracy, cache, throughput, ablation and cited scaling results do not measure a version of the claim. The paper does not fit scaling laws or test predictions from smaller runs.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture proposal paper (Hymba). Its matched-size perplexity tables (Tab. 3, Tab. 9) benchmark the authors' own architecture against architecture families: pure Mamba, Mamba w/ FFN, Llama3-style transformer and Samba. V4 concerns transformer shape (depth, width, heads) at fixed parameter count, not swapping the sequence-mixing operator (SSM vs attention). These are therefore the study's own method compared with others, not a test of V4. No power laws are fitted, nothing is extrapolated, there is no compute-optimal sweep, and no downstream-vs-scale relation is reported. Kaplan et al. is cited only in related work, for transformer 'scalability'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that Hymba, a parallel attention+SSM hybrid-head model with meta tokens and KV-cache optimizations, outperforms other architectures trained under identical settings on most tasks. They also say Hymba-1.5B beats sub-2B public models with much smaller cache and higher throughput. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architecture comparison, not a reproduction of the original scaling-law measurements or compute-optimal allocation method; it reports perplexity for several architectures at matched size and training tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported perplexity comparisons vary by architecture, dataset and model size: 1B models use SmolLM-Corpus, while 300M models use FineWeb.

fits_no_version.finding: At matched parameters, layers, data and recipe, swapping the sequence-mixing architecture family changes perplexity. At 1B, LMB ppl ranges from 10.38 (Hymba) to 14.43 (Mamba2 w/ FFN), and Wiki ppl from 18.62 to 20.42. At 300M, LMB ppl ranges 15.45 to 23.64 and Wiki ppl 28.53 to 33.41. Mamba, Samba and Llama3 are within a few percent on Wiki ppl.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count and training tokens, the choice of architecture family (attention, SSM, hybrid) changes held-out perplexity by up to roughly 30-50% on LAMBADA, beyond the small effects attributed to transformer shape.

record.problems: Only two matched architecture-comparison settings are reported for these perplexity measures. Architecture families are compared rather than depth and width being varied independently; no uncertainty estimates are reported, and the paper does not fit power laws.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows relevant to the tested version were left out.

untested.parts: No variation of depth, width, heads or other transformer shape at fixed parameter count with loss measured. Attention:Mamba ratio ablations (Tab. 10) report task accuracy, not loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 labels are dropped. The rows compare architecture families in the authors' own-method benchmark, not transformer shape. The record's states (e.g. Hymba 'partial') had no coherent basis. The peer_reviewed field 'ICLR 2024' looks wrong: the text is a Nov 2024 arXiv v1 with no venue stated. No uncertainty is reported. The 1B and 300M comparisons use different datasets (SmolLM-Corpus vs FineWeb) and schedules.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss versus parameters, tokens or compute; no scaling-law fit.
No small-run fit or prediction of much larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
The paper compares architecture families, not isolated depth, width and other architectural variables across a wide range.
No other modalities or the listed alternative training regimes are tested for power-law form.
Downstream task results are reported, but the paper does not test predictable downstream performance from scale or pretraining loss.
No exponent or compute-optimal split fitting choices are compared, and no scaling curve is fit.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Mamba and Samba comparisons against Llama3 in the matched-size settings
reader_labels.reason: Their reported Wiki and LMB perplexities are generally close to the Llama3 reference in these comparisons (rows T3-1B-Mamba-Wiki, T3-1B-Mamba-LMB, T3-1B-Samba-Wiki, T3-1B-Samba-LMB, T9-300M-Mamba-Wiki, T9-300M-Mamba-LMB, T9-300M-Samba-LMB).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Mamba w/ FFN and Hymba comparisons, and the 300M Samba Wiki result
reader_labels.reason: Some architecture choices produce noticeably different perplexities from Llama3, especially Mamba w/ FFN and Hymba on LMB perplexity, rather than only slight changes (rows T3-1B-MambaFFN-Wiki, T3-1B-MambaFFN-LMB, T3-1B-Hymba-LMB, T9-300M-MambaFFN-Wiki, T9-300M-MambaFFN-LMB, T9-300M-Samba-Wiki, T9-300M-Hymba-LMB).
